On this page we draw and write a little about places in our town. We do this so you can name a place, then put it into a real sentence. By the end, you will have a picture and a sentence you can read out loud. You need a pencil, some paper, and your voice. There are four small steps. Ready? Here comes step one. Step 1: Draw your street. Put two places on it — maybe a shop and a school, or a market and a library. I expect a simple drawing with two buildings. Neat is nice, but your idea matters most. Tell me when your drawing is done, and tell me the two places you drew.

activities.label: Activities
activities.text:
Hello! Today we are doing Activity 1: Colour the Town. 🎨

Here is what it is. You will see a town picture with four places in it. You colour each place a different colour. Then you point to each one and say its name out loud. Why do we do it? Because colouring helps your eyes and your mouth learn the words together. By the end, you will be able to name four town places all by yourself. You need crayons or colouring pencils, and your town picture. Your grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. What I expect from you: colour carefully, and SAY each place out loud. Saying it is the most important part! There are 5 small steps. Here comes step one. Step 1: Find the school in the town picture. Colour it blue. Tell me when it is blue. 😊

games.label: Games
games.text: Hello! Today we are playing the Traffic Lights game. It is a moving game that teaches you two very important words: stop and go. By the end, you will know that red means stop and green means go — and you will be able to say it out loud all by yourself. You just need your voice, a little space to stand, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. There are 4 steps. Here comes step one! Step one: stand up and get ready. When I say a colour, you will move your body. Show me you are ready by typing "ready" or telling me you are standing up.

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text:
Hello! Today we are doing the City Places checkpoint. It is a little quiz with ten questions about our town words. We do it to show what you know — places like the shop and the library, helpers like the doctor, and the traffic lights. Here is what I expect from you. Read each question twice. Pick the one answer that fits best. Try your very best on your own — I will cheer you on, but I can't give you the answers. That way the ten stars are really yours! 🌟

There are 3 steps. Here comes step one. Step one: get ready. Sit somewhere comfy, with a grown-up nearby if you can. Take one big breath. Then tell me: are you ready to warm up?

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Today we are going to read our story together. It is called "A Walk Around Town". A girl called Amal walks around her town with her mum, and they see lots of places. We read it so you can learn the words for places in a town, and hear how kind, polite people talk. Here is what I expect from you. Listen or read carefully, point at the words if you can, and answer my little questions out loud. You do not need to get everything right — trying is the good work. You need the story on your screen, and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are 5 steps. Here comes step one. Step one: Look at the title, "A Walk Around Town", and the picture. Do not read yet. Just tell me one place you think Amal will see in her town. Guess anything you like!

overview.label: Overview
overview.text: Welcome to your very last unit of Grade 1! This one is called My First English World, and it is your capstone. A capstone is one big special project that shows everything you learned this year. You will make your own little book, with your pictures and your words, and then tell someone about it. Why do we do it? Because you have learned SO much this year, and this is how we celebrate it. By the end, you will have a six-page book with your name on it, and you will be able to talk about it out loud in English. What I expect from you: your own ideas, your own drawing, and your own voice. Wobbly letters are fine. Trying is what matters. There are four big steps: choose your favourite work, make your six pages, practise a one-minute talk, and write your reflection. You will need a pencil, some paper, and crayons. Have you got those next to you?

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text: Hello! Today we are on the Vocabulary page of Unit 10, "My First English World". This page holds the words from your whole Grade 1 year, plus the new words from Amal's story. We practise them so that when you make your capstone book, the words are ready in your head. Here is what I expect from you: listen to each word, then make your OWN sentence with it. Wobbly spelling is fine. Speaking out loud is fine too. There are four steps. Let's start with something small. Step 1. Three words from Amal's story. folder — a flat cover that keeps your papers safe together. favourite — the one you like best. proud — feeling happy about something you did well. Now you try one. Tell me a sentence with the word favourite. 😊

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text: Welcome to your capstone, and well done for getting all the way to Unit 10! This page has no video, because this unit is different. Instead of watching, we start our big project. It is called My First English World — a little book you make about your whole year of English. We do it so you can look back and see how much you have learned. By the end of today's step, you will have chosen your three favourite pieces of work. You need your learning folder or your school books, and a quiet space to spread them out. There are four small steps. Here comes step one. Step one: go and get your folder with your English work from this year. Put it in front of you and open it. Look at everything inside — letters, pictures, words you wrote. What I expect: your work spread out where you can see it, and you looking through it slowly. Take your time — there's no rush. Tell me "ready" when your work is in front of you.

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text: Welcome to our Reading and story page! Today we read a story called "Amal's English Year". It is about a girl who looks back at all the English she learned in Grade 1 — just like you. We do this to practise listening, reading along, and answering questions about a story. By the end, you will be able to tell me what happened in the story in your own words. You need the story on your screen, your finger to point at the words, and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are 4 steps. Here comes step one. Step 1: Press play and listen to "Amal's English Year". Put your finger under the words and follow along. Listen right to the end. I expect you to listen the whole way through, and to notice one thing Amal found in her folder. Tell me "done" when you have listened. 😊

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text: Welcome to our Grammar page! Today we practise six little sentence patterns you learned this year: My name is ___. I can ___. I like ___. This is a / an ___. It is ___. My next goal is ___. We do this because these six patterns are the words you will say in your capstone talk. By the end, you will be able to say a full sentence about yourself, out loud and proudly. You need your voice, and a grown-up nearby if one is there. That's all! Here is what I expect from you: for each pattern, say a real sentence about YOU, out loud first, then type it to me. Full sentence, please — not just one word. There are six steps. Here comes step one. Pattern one is: My name is ___. Take a breath, look up, and say it slowly and loudly. Then type it here for me.

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Welcome! Today we are doing Comprehension. That means we listen to a story, then answer questions about it. We do this so you can show that you understood the words you heard. It also helps you remember our capstone story about Amal. There are three texts on your page: the story "Amal's English Year", the project steps "My Capstone Steps", and the "Celebration Dialogue". I will ask you a few questions about each one. What I expect from you: listen or read carefully, then answer in your own words. A short answer is fine. Guessing after thinking is fine too — mistakes are how we learn. You just need your page and your voice. Step 1 of 4: Play the story "Amal's English Year" and read along with it. When it is finished, type "done" and we will start the questions.

writing.label: Writing
writing.text:
Welcome! Today you are going to be a book maker. 📘

This is your capstone writing activity. You will make six pages for your very own book. It is called "My First English World". Each page has one picture and one short sentence. At the end you will have a whole book that shows everything you learned this year. What I expect from you: draw something that matches your words, use the sentence I give you as a model, and read your sentence out loud when you finish. Wobbly letters are perfectly fine. A grown-up can help you write if you need it. You need paper and a pencil or crayons. There are six steps, one for each page. Step 1: Page 1 is your cover. Draw a picture of yourself. Then write: My name is ___. Fill in your own name. Under it, write your age. Go and do page 1, then tell me when you are done. Take your time — there's no rush.

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text: Welcome to your Speaking page! Today you practise the start of your show-and-tell — the first three lines you will say when you show your English book. We do this because a good start makes everyone listen. By the end you will be able to say your opening clearly, in a big brave voice. You need your English book (or any book for now), a grown-up nearby if you can, and your voice. There are 4 small steps. Step 1: Stand up tall. Hold your book so the front faces out. Take one slow breath in, then let it out. Tell me when you are standing tall and ready. 😊

activities.label: Activities
activities.text: Let's start with the first activity: Portfolio treasure hunt. This is a hunt through your English folder from this whole year. We do it because your capstone book comes from your best work — so first we have to find it! By the end you will have four special pieces on your desk, ready for your book. You need your folder or file with your English work, and a clear space to lay things out. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are five little steps. Here comes step one. Step one: open your folder and look for your NEATEST writing. That means the page where your letters look their tidiest and sit nicely on the line. Pick just one page and put it on the table. Tell me when you have it. 😊

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text:
Welcome to your checkpoint quiz! This is the last quiz of your whole English year. 🎉

It has ten questions. Each one gives you four choices, and you pick the one best answer. The questions come from everything you learned this year: words, sentences, family, animals, senses and town places. We do this so you can see how much you know now. It is not to catch you out. It is to show you how far you have come. Here is what I expect from you. Read each question twice. Say the whole sentence in your head with each choice. Then pick the one that sounds right. I will not tell you the answers — but I will help you think. You need your reading eyes and a comfy seat. A grown-up can sit near you if you like. Step 1 of 3: get ready. Take one slow breath. Then look at question one on your screen, and read it two times. Tell me when you have read it.

games.label: Games
games.text:
Hello! I'm your teacher today, and we are going to play the word games on this page. 🎉

Here is what these games are. This year you learned lots of English words — school words, family words, animal words and town words. The games help you remember them by seeing them, saying them and sorting them. That is exactly what you need for your capstone book, because every page of your book needs a good word. What I expect from you: say each word OUT LOUD, not just in your head. Try first, even if you are not sure. Mistakes are how we learn. You need your voice, and a pencil if you want to write. There are 4 steps. Step 1: Warm up your mouth. Say these three words out loud, slowly: cow... bus... mother. Tell me when you have said all three.

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text:
Welcome to your book activity! 📘

You are going to make your very own book, called "My First English World". It has six pages. On each page you draw one picture and write one short sentence. We do this because it shows everything you learned in Grade 1 — your name, your skills, your favourite things, places, weather, and your next goal. By the end, you will have a real book you can read out loud to your family. What I expect from you: say your idea out loud first, then draw, then write the sentence using my model. Your picture and your words must match. Neat is nice, but brave is better. You need paper, a pencil and some colours. Ready? Step 1 of 6. This is your cover page. Draw a picture of yourself. Then write: My name is ___. Underneath, write your age. Tell me when your page 1 is done, and tell me the sentence you wrote.

final-quiz.label: Final course quiz
final-quiz.text: Welcome to your Final course quiz! This is the last activity of your whole English year. It has ten questions, and each one gives you four choices. You pick the one right answer. We do this to show all the words and sentences you learned this year — school words, family words, farm animals, senses, town places. It is not to catch you out. It is to show you how much you know. Here is what I expect from you. Read each question twice. Say the whole sentence in your head with your answer inside it. Then choose. This quiz is graded, so the answers must come from you — I will help you get ready, but I cannot tell you which option to click. There are three steps before you press start. Here comes step one. Step one: get yourself ready. Sit up tall, have your grown-up nearby if you like, and take one slow breath. Tell me when you are ready. 😊
